summary: Working on auth module storage decisions

message.content: We need to pick a storage layer for the sync server. I'm thinking Postgres but it feels heavy for an MVP. What do you think? Context: this is a small self-hosted service that teams run in Docker, mostly storing presence pings and handoff bundles. Write volume is low, maybe a few events per second at peak for a large team. We want the Docker image to stay small and the setup to be zero-config for evaluators. Operational simplicity matters more than raw throughput here, and we should avoid anything that needs a separate database container for the default path.

content.text: For an MVP self-hosted service with low write volume, SQLite is the better default: zero-config, single file, ships inside the Docker image. Postgres adds a second container and migration overhead evaluators will feel immediately. We can keep the storage layer behind an interface so Postgres remains a drop-in option for large teams later.

message.content: Agreed, SQLite as default with a storage interface. Also I hit that weird Windows thing again where spawning .cmd files fails.

content.text: Right — on Windows, Node's spawn() cannot execute .cmd files directly without shell: true since the CVE-2024-27980 patch; it throws EINVAL. Anywhere we spawn the claude CLI we must use shell: true on win32, and keep user input out of the argument list, passing it via stdin instead.

todos.content: Fix spawn shell handling on Windows

message.content: Great. Let's also make sure the API key sk-ant-test12345678901234567890 never ends up in shared notes.

content.text: Understood — secrets never belong in distilled team memory. I'll finish wiring the storage interface now and we can review the diff together before committing. The interface exposes get/put/list/delete over namespaced keys, with the SQLite implementation as the default binding registered at startup.
